skill.name: caveman-optimize
skill.description: Turn Caveman's exact report-only repository observations into an operator-chosen optimization candidate with a paired baseline/candidate evaluation. Use when the user asks to inspect an optimization observation, evaluate a candidate change, or act on the current Caveman optimization report. Require a logged-in Caveman CLI connection and explicit approval; never infer money or actuation from a profile.
skill.summary: Evaluate one operator-selected Caveman observation through an approved candidate change and a controlled baseline comparison.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

content.value_statement: Aggregate repository profiles do not identify a safe or valuable code change by themselves. This skill tests one approved candidate against a controlled baseline.
actual_capabilities: Reads current report-only observations through the Caveman CLI.
Presents supported observations without ranking or invented savings.
Requires an explicit operator choice before inspecting candidate callsites.
Designs one minimal candidate change with a paired baseline evaluation.
Applies only the approved change and runs focused repository checks.
Reports measured results, quality checks, and an adoption decision.
limitations: Requires an authenticated Caveman CLI session.
Supports only the four current repository profile identifiers listed by the skill.
Cannot proceed without a fixed fixture, quality check, and common measurement method.
Does not create experiments, change opportunity lifecycle state, or verify production savings.

use_cases.title: Reduce Context Window Load
use_cases.description: Evaluate a focused code change against a current context-window profile using identical baseline and candidate inputs.

use_cases.title: Control Tool Output Size
use_cases.description: Test whether a specific output reduction preserves task quality while improving the selected resource measure.

use_cases.title: Review Optimization Evidence
use_cases.description: Verify that a proposed optimization has callsite evidence, controlled measurements, and an explicit operator decision.

prompt_templates.title: List Current Observations
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the current Caveman report-only observations. Show supported items with their exact identifiers, titles, observations, and last-seen times. Do not rank them.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before choosing an optimization area.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect One Observation
prompt_templates.prompt: I choose [observation id]. Inspect the repository for one evidenced callsite that could produce this profile. Do not edit any files yet.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused investigation after an operator selects an observation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Paired Evaluation
prompt_templates.prompt: For [observation id], propose one minimal candidate and a paired baseline evaluation. Specify the fixture, quality check, resource measure, commands, environment, and confounders.

prompt_templates.title: Apply and Assess a Candidate
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the approved candidate for [observation id]. Run the paired evaluation and focused checks. Keep it only if quality and resource evidence support adoption.

output: The skill lists each supported observation with its exact server title and recorded profile.
It asks the operator to select one item before repository inspection.
The report identifies one evidenced callsite and the approved minimal change.
It compares baseline and candidate results on the same fixture and measurement.
It records quality checks, code checks, accounting limits, and the final decision.

best_practices: Refresh observations through the authenticated CLI before every evaluation.
Use identical fixed inputs and the same resource measurement for both evaluation arms.
Approve the candidate and evaluation design before editing repository files.
anti_patterns: Do not infer dollars, savings, or production impact from aggregate profiles.
Do not use retired identifiers or historical proposals as current evidence.
Do not keep a candidate when quality regresses or the comparison is inconclusive.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically optimize my repository?
faq.answer: No. It requires an operator-selected observation and approval before applying one minimal candidate.

faq.question: Which observations are supported?
faq.answer: It supports context-window-profile, tool-catalog-profile, tool-output-size-profile, and exploration-load-profile.

faq.question: Does it estimate financial savings?
faq.answer: No. It reports a zero opportunity band and does not convert local resource reductions into money.

faq.question: What happens when Caveman authentication fails?
faq.answer: The workflow stops without editing and reports the exact blocker.

faq.question: Can ordinary unit tests prove the optimization?
faq.answer: No. The evaluation also needs a fixed fixture, a quality check, and a shared resource measurement.

faq.question: Can the skill change Caveman opportunity state?
faq.answer: No. It does not create experiments, proposals, lifecycle changes, dismissals, or optimizer activation.
